options: Fixed-size and non-overlapping — every event belongs to exactly one window, and windows tile back-to-back with no gaps
Fixed-size but overlapping windows

The join kind=leftouter operator

questions.q: Why is a tumbling window the cheapest window shape to compute?
options: Each event is touched by exactly one window, and no window needs to be recomputed once it closes
It requires no aggregation logic at all
It only works on batch-ingested data, which is always cheaper
It skips storing any data
questions.explain: No overlap means no event is ever double-counted or reprocessed across windows.

questions.q: Why can't a tumbling window show a dashboard counter that updates smoothly every minute instead of jumping every 5?
options: Each tumbling window only closes and reports once every 5 minutes, so there's no partial or rolling update in between
Tumbling windows update continuously by definition
Dashboards can't display tumbling window results at all
